title: Official publicly published lift-station register
coverage: 131 agency-published Current-register lift stations: 82 City-owned/maintained and 49 privately owned. Default City-only view is an ownership filter, not a city-limit or service-area boundary.

sources.title: City of St. Petersburg Water Resources · PublicWastewater · Sewer Lift Station
sources.updateNote: Service description says approximately monthly updates; GIS inventory status is not live operating status.

sources.title: Pinellas County · public Know Your Zone parcel evacuation-zone layer
sources.method: Exact point-in-polygon on official source parcel geometry. Only polygons intersecting agency-published station points were downloaded; no address or parcel-owner fields retained.

sources.title: USGS 3DEP Elevation Point Query Service · interpolated bare-earth terrain
sources.method: At each agency-published station point, USGS EPQS returned terrain elevation in feet, source raster ID, resolution and acquisition date. Vertical datum independently verified against the public 3DEP ImageServer catalog for every returned raster. No ground direction is inferred for pumped flow.

completeness.zoneIndependentPointQueryAgreement: 131/131; source points independently queried against the official County layer

limitations: Public asset inventory and mapped evacuation-zone intersections only. This is not a real-time station status, flood-depth, outage, evacuation-order or facility-safety feed.

City ownership/maintenance is distinct from municipal limits, Pinellas County Utilities ownership and wastewater-service boundaries. Privately owned records here are already published by the City; ownership is labeled and never presented as a City-owned asset.

The City register itself has no ground-elevation field. Added USGS3DEP values are separately sourced, interpolated terrain (2007 / 2018–2019 acquisition), not current surveyed asset/equipment height; no pipe invert or cover elevation was substituted.
No verified station-to-station dependency graph is included. Geometry and From/To node fields in public mains layers alone do not establish a complete operational flow model or failure propagation.

Evacuation zones are planning classifications based on storm-surge risk, distinct from FEMA flood zones and event-specific evacuation orders. A no-intersection, boundary or ambiguous result is unknown, never a non-evacuation or safe classification.
Station points and parcel evacuation polygons can differ at boundaries/rights-of-way. Confirm current location-specific instructions in the official County lookup.
The City provides this public data as is without guarantees of accuracy, timeliness or completeness; conclusions are the user’s responsibility.
